name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Sheri Biggs running with large fundraising edge
Democrat Eunice Lehmacher raised only ~$41K with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The district's R+21 lean, Biggs's incumbency, and her roughly 12-to-1 fundraising advantage over Lehmacher leave Democrats with no evident path; markets price a Republican win near certainty. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move materially off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Biggs or a major scandal would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, and first-term incumbent Sheri Biggs is running for reelection with the advantages that typically come with it. She has raised over $500,000 and holds more than $200,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Eunice Lehmacher has raised about $41,000, with no outside spending on either side. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Biggs roughly a 95% chance of winning. The district's strong partisan lean and the fundraising gap make an upset very unlikely, and the forecast places this race firmly in the Safe Republican category.
